chapter: Teddy Wilson bands and Cafe Society
title: Dismissed with Bill Coleman as too international
summary: Barney Josephson would only rehire Teddy Wilson without Hall and Coleman because of their interracial associations.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So then we came back to New York, we were out of work for a while and Teddy, in scrounging for another job, Barney Josephson Bobby (inaudible) didn't want Bill Coleman and me --
Why?
Because we were inseparable and the readout was that we were too international because we were --
What do you mean, too international?
Bill had, you know, come from Paris and you know, interracial associations.
In other words, you were being too relaxed with everyone instead of --
So Teddy could get the job back if he didn't have us.
Yeah. You weren't keeping your places, in other words?
Right.
You know, I hadn't thought of that expression for a long time there.
So then it was Teddy Wilson and Mousiey Alexander and -- [g.v.]
I didn't realize Mousie played in the Teddy --
And Big Sid Catlett
Well, Mousie and Sid were both drummers so --
Oh, no, Mousie Randolph.
Randolph, right, trumpet player. Big Sid.
Big Sid, and who was playing drums, I guess Bennie, maybe Bennie was.
Well, who took your place?
Johnny Williams.
Was he married to Mary Lou or is that --
No, no, no, no.
That's that saxophone player.
Yeah, yeah.
Did you have a falling out with Teddy about this or you thought he was in the position where he couldn't do anything?
No, I didn't have a falling out with him. We were all scuffling trying to get a job, you know, and --
So what did you and Bill do?
Scuffled. Tried to get a job.
